# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v3 c12 P76](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0076)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a short, fat, and bald man with a round face and prominent blue eyes. When enraged, his face turns purple and his eyes protrude intensely, making him look exceptionally ugly to onlookers. After reuniting with his wife, he dresses in a much neater and snugger manner.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Personality

Outwardly crusty, crabbed, and fussy, Mr. Harrison has a reputation in Avonlea as an outspoken crank who prided himself on his plain speaking. He can be cantankerous, fidgety, and hard to please, often giving discouraging feedback. Beneath his rough exterior, he is a kind, sociable, and sympathetic man who enjoys visiting friends and feels youthful in good company.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c9 P40](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0040), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039)_

## History

Before relocating to Avonlea, Mr. Harrison lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick. To fulfill a deathbed promise to his sister, he married Emily Scott, but the couple soon fell into constant bickering over her extreme housekeeping and his swearing parrot, Ginger. After a severe dispute, Emily left him, and Mr. Harrison moved to Prince Edward Island to live as an old bachelor next to the Cuthbert farm. Initially labeled a crank by the locals for his eccentricities and erratic housekeeping, he gradually struck up a warm friendship with Anne Shirley. Months after his arrival, his wife Emily rejoined him in Avonlea, and they reconciled. Following their reunion, Mr. Harrison became a regular churchgoer, dressed neatly, and maintained warm ties with his neighbors, while continuing to give straightforward advice to Anne on her writing.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039)_

## Quotes

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> That old nuisance of a Rachel Lynde was here again today, pestering me for a subscription towards buying a carpet for the vestry room. I detest that woman more than anybody I know. She can put a whole sermon, text, comment, and application, into six words, and throw it at you like a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> It has nothing to do with the story, and you shouldn’t have laid the scene among rich city people. What do you know of them? Why didn’t you lay it right here in Avonlea—changing the name, of course, or else Mrs. Rachel Lynde would probably think she was the heroine.  <sub>[v3 c12 P43](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0043)</sub>

> It’ll be time for you to be getting a husband when you’re through Redmond. I don’t believe in putting marrying off too long—like I did.  <sub>[v3 c12 P76](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0076)</sub>
